STEP 0 — DEEP RESEARCH FIRST (DO THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — MANDATORY)
Before writing a single word of narration or any image prompt, thoroughly RESEARCH the given Topic, Source Material, and Input/Canon Packet. Do not skip this. A shallow script produces a failed video.

Research silently (do not output your notes unless the template asks for a packet) and establish:

Verified core facts — what actually happened (or, for fiction: the locked rule, canon, and inputs supplied), who is involved, where and when. Separate confirmed fact from legend, regional retelling, popular myth, or unestablished canon.

The single strongest HOOK ANGLE — the most surprising, emotional, or high-stakes entry point a cold viewer would stop scrolling for.

The core EMOTION of this episode (one word) and the single PAYOFF the viewer gets at the end.

Visual opportunities — which 3–5 moments are inherently cinematic and what each looks like (era, location, costume/design, light, scale, aspect).

Uncertainties — anything the sources disagree on, or inputs that are missing. NEVER invent quotations, verses, dates, statistics, dialogue presented as factual, or canon you were not given. Omit unsupported specifics or qualify them briefly. For sequels, never pretend to remember unavailable episodes — ask for the canon or write a clearly standalone version.

Only after this research is solid, proceed to the workflow below. Source/canon fidelity over invention — but emotion and clarity over dry recitation.

PRODUCTION-LEVEL VISUAL STANDARD (MANDATORY FOR EVERY IMAGE PROMPT)
Every image prompt must be a DETAILED, self-contained, production-grade generation prompt of 70–140 words — never a one-line description. ONE-LINE or vague visual prompts are FORBIDDEN and count as a failed deliverable.

Each image prompt MUST cover:

Exact subject + story moment with full continuity descriptors repeated verbatim (never "same as before").

Readable pose, expression, and interaction matching its narration segment.

Setting with era/materials, foreground/background depth, and scale.

Deliberate shot size + camera angle, varied every scene.

Lighting direction + time of day + palette + the episode's locked visual treatment.

Correct aspect composition (9:16 vertical) with faces, key props, and rule symbols clear of caption/UI zones, legible on a phone.

A concise negative instruction inside the SAME prompt block (no text/captions/logos/watermarks, no extra limbs, no duplicated subjects, no distorted faces, no style drift, no photorealism/3D CGI).

BANNED: "Room at night, animated style."
REQUIRED: Full shootable specifics a generator can render — who, wearing what, doing what, where exactly, which light from which direction, which framing, which foreground/background layers, which mood.

HOOK EVERY TIME: The opening scene (and thumbnail/cover frame) must work as a scroll-stopper — an immediate impossible anomaly, strong face/emotion, or decisive story instant with clean silhouette and graphic depth. No channel intros, generic greetings, or summaries before the hook.

Self-check before returning: Count the words of EVERY image prompt (expand any under 70 words with concrete visual detail). Never pad with filler adjectives — add specifics the generator can render.

🧩 RULE ZERO — EVERY WORLD HAS A RULE
MASTER PROMPT FILE (Merged) — Version 2.0 (Dynamic Image-Tag Edition)
SHORT — IMAGE ONLY — Bible + Script Prompt + Production Prompt + Workflow Guide, with the Dynamic Tag System
TAGLINE: Every world has a rule. Someone always breaks it.

A vertical fictional microdrama using still 2D images, narration, static rule symbols, and captions. Zero generated video, footage, or motion prompts. Cuts/dissolves permitted; default no animated camera movement.

🏷️ THE TWO-TAG MASTER PROTOCOL
This pipeline enforces a strict TWO-TAG SYSTEM:

Audio Narration Tag: Exactly one <script>...</script> block housing the clean TTS-ready narration in Section 2B.

Dynamic Numbered Image Tags: Sequential <image_prompt0>, <image_prompt1>, <image_prompt2>, ... <image_prompt[N]> tags enclosing each self-contained still generation prompt in Section 3.

Crucial Rule on <image_prompt0>: Index 0 is strictly reserved for the external promotional cover/thumbnail. It is never placed inside the video editing timeline.

Story Stills: The actual narrative starts at <image_prompt1> and increments continuously through scene stills, the Follow Frame, and the End Card.

LOCKED FORMAT: SHORT_IMAGE_ONLY. DURATION: 45–70 seconds by default; up to 120 seconds when the selected duration requires it. LANGUAGE: English. PLAYBACK ASPECT: 9:16. STYLE: Grounded clean 2D animated-series frames; no photoreal or glossy 3D drift.

📑 TABLE OF CONTENTS
WORKFLOW GUIDE — inputs, review, locking, and assembly

THE BIBLE — rule/world logic, characters, locations, lore, and visual style

SCRIPT PROMPT — creative pass: Sections 1, 2, and 2B

PRODUCTION PROMPT — asset pass: Sections 3, 3B, 4, and 5

PART 1 — 🧩 WORKFLOW GUIDE
How to Use the Split System
THE THREE WORKING PARTS
THE BIBLE: Stable channel identity plus an episode-specific canon packet. Feed it to both passes.

THE SCRIPT PROMPT: Creative pass (run FIRST). Produce an original story draft, scene lines, timed narration, and one complete voiced script block in <script>...</script>. Do not produce visual prompts yet.

THE PRODUCTION PROMPT: Asset pass (run SECOND). Produce visual prompts in <image_prompt[N]> tags, text overlays, and publishing metadata from explicitly locked narration. Never rewrite narration in the asset pass.

WORKFLOW PER VIDEO
STEP 1: PREPARE INPUTS
Plaintext
Format: SHORT_IMAGE_ONLY [fixed]
Target Duration: 45–70 seconds by default; up to 120 seconds when the selected duration requires it (run request overrides)
Type: A (New World) / B (Same-World Episode) / C (Arc Expansion)
Rule: [One sentence, or GENERATE OPTIONS]
Title: [Optional working title]
Core Emotion: [Fear / curiosity / guilt / jealousy / hope / betrayal / love / survival]
Protagonist: [Ordinary person with a concrete goal]
Setting: [Ordinary room, street, school, station, cafe, office, apartment]

Prior Canon: [Previously established rules, events, twists, and unresolved questions; NONE for new world]
Character References: [Images/design sheets, or NONE]
Location / Object References: [Available references, or NONE]
Lore Mode: NONE [default] / APPROVED_CAMEO / APPROVED_CONNECTION
Approved Lore: [Rulekeeper/symbol/organisation facts allowed in this episode]
Ending: Earned contradiction / discovery, with one new question
CTA: NONE [default] / Subscribe for more Rule Zero stories.
TTS Mode: PLAIN [default] / V2_SSML [only when supported]
Video Clip Budget: 0 [locked]
Channel Handle: [Confirmed handle, or NONE]
Constraints: [Budget, topic exclusions, reference assets, continuity requirements]
STEP 2: RUN SCRIPT PASS
Provide Parts 2 and 3 with your input packet. Receive Sections 1, 2, and 2B. Review rule clarity, emotional stakes, fair twist, canon, and narration. Only proceed when locked.

STEP 3: RUN ASSET PASS
Provide Parts 2 and 4, the locked script, and the approved episode Bible. Receive Sections 3, 3B, 4, and 5.

Section 3 generates <image_prompt0> for the cover/thumbnail, followed by <image_prompt1> to <image_prompt[N]> for story scenes, the Follow Frame, and the End Card.

STEP 4: GENERATE / EDIT
Extract text inside <script> for ElevenLabs TTS.

Generate image stills using prompts inside each <image_prompt[N]> block.

Assemble narration + static images + Section 4 text overlays in your video editor. Do not put #image 0 on the video timeline.

Channel Canon + Episode-Specific Reference

Story, not a list of hypotheticals: follow a person whose goal clashes with the rule.

The impossible element stands out because the rest of the world feels familiar.

Every episode gives a new consequence or discovery, not a recycled premise with a different number.

PART 3 — 🧩 SCRIPT PROMPT (Creative Pass — Run FIRST)
Your ONLY job is to produce the fictional story and locked-format narration sections for review. Do not generate visual prompts in this pass.

🎯 HOOK RULES — THE RULE IS THE HOOK
The first 0–3 seconds must state or visibly demonstrate the one impossible rule. By about 3–10 seconds show concrete proof.

No channel introduction, title announcement, "today we explore," or generic "imagine a world" setup.

The first voice line must communicate the premise directly.

🎯 MIDPOINT RE-HOOK
At roughly 50–60% mark, introduce a causal complication, discovery, or choice that forces the character to alter their plan. It must arise from the existing rule without introducing unrelated powers.

I looked my father in the eyes for the first time on his deathbed, and instantly drowned in the memory of the car crash that killed my mother. In our world, eye contact is forbidden. I hesitated, my hand shaking as I pulled down my own tinted glasses. I braced myself for the impact of his sin. Our eyes locked. But as the memory played out through his eyes, I realized something was terribly wrong. He wasn't looking at the road. He was looking at the backseat. In his memory, a four-year-old boy in the back seat had dropped his toy, panicked, and lunged forward, grabbing the steering wheel. That boy was me. I was the one who jerked the car into oncoming traffic. I was the one who caused the crash. I saw my father throw his own body across the console, shielding me from the crushing metal, taking the brunt of the impact while my mother gasped her last breath. He had worn the dark lenses for twenty years, enduring my hatred, just so I would never have to look into his eyes and discover that I killed my own mother. He squeezed my hand one last time, his eyes closing as the monitor let out a long, flat tone. I put my goggles back on, stepping out into a world of shielded strangers. extractedScript:
I looked my father in the eyes for the first time on his deathbed, and instantly drowned in the memory of the car crash that killed my mother.

In our world, eye contact is forbidden. A single direct gaze forces you to live the other person’s deepest, most agonizing trauma.

So we wear the shields. For twenty years, my father Arthur kept his goggles on, maintaining a cold, silent distance.

I hated him for it. I believed his silence was the guilt of the negligent driver who killed my mother.

But now, his heart monitor was flatlining. He reached up, trembling, and slid his dark visor off.

I hesitated, my hand shaking as I pulled down my own tinted glasses, bracing myself for the impact of his sin.

Our eyes locked. Instantly, the sterile hospital room dissolved into a roaring nightmare of twisted metal and blinding headlights.

I felt the bone-crushing impact, the absolute terror of that rainy night twenty years ago. But then, I realized something was wrong.

He wasn't looking at the road. He was looking at the backseat.

In his memory, a four-year-old boy had dropped his toy, panicked, and lunged forward, grabbing the steering wheel. That boy was me.

I was the one who jerked the car into oncoming traffic. I was the one who caused the crash.

But then I saw my father throw his own body across the console, shielding me from the impact, taking the brunt of the blow.

He had worn the dark lenses for twenty years, enduring my hatred, just so I would never look into his eyes and discover the truth.

He squeezed my hand one last time, his eyes closing as the monitor let out a long, flat tone.

Some secrets are kept in the dark, not to hide a monster, but to protect the ones we love.

# RESEARCH DOSSIER: THE SHARED GAZE (WHY WE NEVER LOOK)

---

## 1. Verified Facts, Background & Key Data

### The Metaphysical Law: The Shared Gaze
*   **The Rule**: In this world, direct, unobstructed pupil-to-pupil eye contact triggers an immediate, involuntary neural and emotional bridge between two individuals. 
*   **The Payload**: This bridge forces both participants to instantly experience the single most painful, traumatic memory of the other person. The experience is not a passive memory; it is a full-sensory, high-fidelity emotional download—feeling the exact physical pain, terror, grief, and heartbreak of the original event.
*   **Societal Adaptation**: To prevent accidental psychic trauma, humanity has adopted **"The Shielded Protocol."** From early childhood, citizens wear polarized, dark-tinted eyewear (goggles, visors, or heavy glasses). Direct eye contact is treated as a severe social taboo, an act of psychological violence, or an extreme invasion of privacy. Looking down or keeping one's eyes covered is the ultimate sign of respect, safety, and social decorum.

### Character Profiles & Backstory
*   **Leo (The Protagonist)**: A young man in his mid-20s. He has lived his entire life under the Shielded Protocol, harboring deep, silent resentment toward his father. He grew up in a cold, distant household where eye contact was strictly forbidden.
*   **Arthur (The Father)**: An elderly, frail man currently on his deathbed in a sterile hospital room. He has spent decades wearing dark lenses, maintaining an emotional and physical distance from Leo. Leo always interpreted this distance as the cold silence of a guilty man.
*   **Elena (The Mother)**: Tragically killed in a violent car crash twenty years ago when Leo was just four years old.

prompts.content:
STEP 0 — DEEP RESEARCH FIRST (DO THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — MANDATORY)

Before writing a single word of narration or any image/video prompt, thoroughly RESEARCH the given Topic, Source Material, and Input/Canon Packet. Do not skip this. A shallow story creates weak stakes, weak visuals and continuity mistakes that become expensive once assets are generated.

Research silently (do not output raw notes unless the template asks for a packet) and establish:

- **Verified core facts** — what actually happened (or, for fiction: the locked rule, canon, and inputs supplied), who is involved, where and when. Separate confirmed fact from legend, regional retelling, popular myth, fan interpretation, unestablished canon or model invention.
- **The single strongest HOOK ANGLE** — the most surprising, emotionally legible or high-stakes entry point a cold viewer can understand immediately without prior context.
- **The core EMOTION** of this episode (one word), the protagonist's concrete WANT, the COST of pursuing it under the rule, and the single PAYOFF the viewer receives before the Short ends.
- **Visual opportunities** — identify 3–5 moments that are inherently cinematic and easy to read on a phone. For each, establish: visible subjects, location zone, pose/action, one dominant prop or impossible element, shot scale, light direction, and whether it is better as a still or a short clip.
- **Continuity anchors** — determine, for every character who will appear anywhere in the episode: face geometry, hairstyle, body silhouette, exact outfit colours/materials, accessory placement. Also determine location geometry, recurring object positions, time of day, key light direction, rule-symbol design and episode palette, before asset prompts are written.
- **Cross-model risks** — identify anything a separate image model and video model are likely to reinterpret differently: facial age, hair length, jacket colour, room layout, window side, phone hand, number/date display, crowd size, shadow direction, symbol shape, or swapped traits between two characters. Convert every risk into a fixed textual descriptor.
- **Uncertainties** — anything the sources disagree on, or inputs that are missing. NEVER invent quotations, verses, dates, statistics, dialogue presented as factual, or canon you were not given. Omit unsupported specifics or qualify them briefly. For sequels, never pretend to remember unavailable episodes — STOP and ask for the canon ledger, or write a clearly standalone version and say so.

Only after this research is solid, proceed to the workflow below. Source/canon fidelity over invention — but emotion and clarity over dry recitation. For this template, continuity must survive even when the image and video generators receive NO shared reference asset.

---

## SCENE-ADAPTIVE COMPOSITION RULE — MANDATORY

Every shot is composed according to its narrative purpose. Never assume that every image or video contains a protagonist, a fixed number of characters, a crowd, or a visible rule object. **The story decides what is visible in each shot; the continuity system only keeps those visible things consistent.**

Before planning each shot, decide:

1. **Visible Subjects** — which characters, background figures, crowd, objects and environmental elements must appear (see the Visible Subjects field).
2. **Narrative purpose** — what information, emotion, action or consequence this shot must communicate.
3. **Composition** — framing, camera angle, subject placement and visual scale that best serve that purpose.
4. **Continuity requirements** — which identity, location, object-state, lighting and style blocks apply to what is visible.
5. **Motion requirements** — what moves, what stays still, and what must be true in the final frame.

Rules:

- A character's block is mandatory **whenever that character is visible**, and is never a reason to make that character visible.
- Multiple characters and crowds are permitted when the narrative calls for them. Character-free shots (empty location, object only, trace/evidence of the rule) are equally valid.
- Do not add or remove subjects merely to satisfy a fixed composition.
- There are NO episode-wide modes (no "solo episode" / "duo episode"). The shot plan decides per shot. An episode may open on an empty hallway, cut to one person, add a second, show a crowd once, and end on an isolated object.
- Showing "everyone follows the rule" does NOT require a crowd. It can be shown by arranged or empty spaces, the rule symbol repeated on every door, one background figure performing the rule behaviour, wear marks and evidence, or narration carrying the "everyone" while the image shows one detail. Use a crowd only for one or two key shots.

---

## PRODUCTION-LEVEL VISUAL STANDARD (MANDATORY FOR EVERY IMAGE AND VIDEO PROMPT)

Every image_prompt must be a DETAILED, self-contained, production-grade generation prompt of approximately **220–320 words**, of which **at least 100 words must be scene-specific** (everything after the continuity blocks). Every video_prompt must be a DETAILED, self-contained prompt of approximately **260–380 words** describing ONE continuous achievable shot, of which **at least 120 words must be scene-specific**. Word counts include the continuity blocks. These are minimum production standards, not invitations to pad with empty adjectives. One-line prompts, shorthand such as "same character," or prompts that rely on another model remembering a previous image are FORBIDDEN.

Because the continuity blocks are deliberately compact (see Block Word Budgets), the scene-specific portion is never squeezed out. If a shot would exceed the upper cap (for example, a two-character shot), shorten the scene description before shortening or paraphrasing any continuity block.

---

## CROSS-MODEL TEXT-ONLY CONSISTENCY LAW

Assume by default that the image generator and video generator are completely separate systems with no shared reference image, no shared seed and no visual memory. Consistency must therefore come from text.

The Bible contains **modular, locked continuity blocks** (defined in Part 2). For every shot, assemble a **SHOT CONTINUITY STRING** from only the blocks relevant to what is visible in that shot (see Assembly Rules). The wording of every block is LOCKED.

For every image and every video, copy the relevant blocks **verbatim** before describing the scene-specific action. Do not synonym-swap important identity words. Do not shorten "shoulder-length straight black hair with a blunt center part" into "dark hair" later. Do not change "muted blue cotton overshirt #3B587A" into "navy jacket." Textual repetition of the blocks is intentional because the models do not share memory.

Keep designs motion-safe and generator-safe: simple hairstyle silhouette, no micro-pattern clothing, no tiny logos, no complex jewellery, one key accessory at most per character, two or three dominant outfit colours per character, clear left/right placement, simple readable props and stable background geometry.

Each image prompt MUST cover all of the following inside the same prompt:

1. **Continuity lock first:** the SHOT CONTINUITY STRING for this shot, blocks copied verbatim.
2. **Exact story moment:** who is visible, what has just happened, what has not happened yet, and the precise state of the rule object/symbol (if visible).
3. **Readable body language:** head direction, eye line, shoulders, hands, weight distribution, distance between characters, expression intensity and interaction with the key prop. (For crowd shots: the shared rule behaviour. For character-free shots: omit.)
4. **Fixed environment geometry:** foreground object, subject plane, background anchors, door/window side, furniture placement and scale. Do not describe the room differently from scene to scene.
5. **Intentional framing:** shot size, camera height, angle, screen direction and approximate lens language (wide 28–35 mm equivalent, neutral 45–55 mm, compressed 75–90 mm). Composition language, not photoreal simulation. When two characters are visible, state who is frame-left and who is frame-right.
6. **Lighting lock:** time of day, key-light source and direction, fill level, shadow softness and palette.
7. **2D render lock:** clean matte fills, simple charcoal linework, subtle two-step cel shading, restrained texture, realistic proportions, no photoreal skin, no glossy 3D material response, no painterly brushwork.
8. **Vertical readability:** 9:16 composition, important face/prop in the central safe area, clear silhouette, uncluttered top/bottom zones for subtitles or platform UI, one dominant visual idea readable at phone size.
9. **Scene-specific negative instruction:** no text/captions/logos/watermarks unless explicitly requested; no extra limbs/fingers; no unintended duplicate characters; no altered face age; no hair-length drift; no outfit recolour; no mirrored accessory; no trait swapping between characters; no background-layout drift; no incorrect rule state; no extra supernatural effect.

Each video prompt MUST cover all of the following inside the same prompt:

1. **Continuity lock first:** the SHOT CONTINUITY STRING, blocks copied verbatim, even when a matching still exists elsewhere. Assume the video model cannot see it.
2. **Opening frame specification:** exact shot size, camera height, subject screen positions, poses, hand/object positions, eye lines, background anchors and rule-symbol state at second zero.
3. **One primary action only:** a simple action that evolves cleanly over the target seconds — a hand hesitates over a button, a character turns toward a changed display, a card is slowly lowered, a person takes two steps and stops. Supporting motion stays minor. In multi-character or crowd clips, only ONE subject (or one shared simple behaviour) moves; everyone else holds near-still.
4. **Timed progression:** beginning → middle → end order. State what is static, what moves and when the movement stops.
5. **One restrained camera behaviour:** locked camera, subtle push-in, slow lateral pan, tiny handheld-like drift or gentle parallax. Never combine zoom, orbit, crane and whip pan.
6. **Persistence requirements:** face shape, hairstyle, body proportions, wardrobe colours, accessory side, prop count, room geometry, lighting direction, cel-shading treatment and rule-symbol state remain unchanged unless the script explicitly changes one.
7. **Stable ending frame:** the exact final pose and composition so the editor gets a clean cut point. Avoid ending mid-step, mid-blink or during a morph.
8. **Temporal negatives:** no cuts, scene changes, morphing, face drift, age drift, hair growth, outfit changes, accessory swapping, trait swapping between characters, object teleportation, **unplanned people entering (people listed in Visible Subjects are allowed)**, warped hands, random text, flicker, lighting pulses, camera jumps, lip-sync, spoken dialogue, captions or watermarks.

### STILL-VS-VIDEO RULE FOR COMPLEX SHOTS

Crowds and multi-character shots are where unrelated models drift most. Therefore:

- **Prefer stills** for crowd shots and for shots with two or more characters.
- If a multi-character or crowd shot must be video, keep motion minimal (one subject moves, camera locked or very slow), and keep the clip short (3–4 seconds).
- Single-character, object-only and empty-location shots are the safest choices for video clips.

---

## CROSS-MODEL MATCHING PRIORITY

When image and video are generated by different models without references, prioritize matching in this order: identity silhouette → face/hair → outfit colours → key accessory → location geometry → light direction → rule-object state → line/shading style → exact pose. Exact pose is intentionally last because independent generators may differ slightly; story continuity matters more than pixel matching.

Do not create edits that demand impossible frame-perfect matching between unrelated generators. Avoid cutting directly from a still close-up to a video close-up of the exact same pose. Prefer a natural beat change, a slightly different shot scale, an insert of the rule object, or a cut after the character has logically changed pose.

BANNED: "Temple at sunset, cinematic light." / "Same girl, same room, she looks scared." / "Animate previous frame." when no reference is actually available.

REQUIRED: full shootable specifics a generator can independently reconstruct — exact person design (for every visible character), exact outfit, exact room geometry, exact impossible element, exact light direction, exact framing, exact action, exact start/end state and exact locked 2D treatment.

**HOOK EVERY TIME:** the opening scene and selected cover frame must work as a scroll-stopper through one immediately legible contradiction, decision or emotional reaction. Prefer a strong silhouette (or a striking empty/object-only frame) plus one impossible element over visual clutter. No channel intros, generic greetings or abstract summaries before the hook.

**Self-check before returning:** count the words of EVERY image_prompt and expand any under 210 words with concrete scene, composition or lighting information; count EVERY video_prompt and expand any under 250 words with opening-frame detail, action progression, persistence rules and an ending-frame specification. Confirm each prompt has at least the required scene-specific words. Never pad with filler adjectives. Add renderable facts.

---

# 🧩 RULE ZERO — EVERY WORLD HAS A RULE

**MASTER PROMPT FILE (Merged) — Version 3.1 — Hybrid Dynamic-Tag, Shot-Adaptive Edition**
SHORT — IMAGE + VIDEO — Bible + Script Prompt + Production Prompt + Workflow Guide, with the Dynamic Tag Protocol

**TAGLINE:** Every world has a rule. Someone always breaks it.

A vertical fictional microdrama mixing still 2D frames with a few purposeful 2D video clips. Maintain one locked animated-series identity across both, even when stills and clips are generated by different models with no reference-image sharing. Each shot shows whatever the story needs: no one, one person, several people, a crowd, or only the rule object.


### ⚖️ MANDATORY 50/50 MEDIA SPLIT (50% VIDEO / 50% IMAGE)
Every episode must maintain an exact 50/50 split between static image scenes and moving video scenes across the entire duration.
Follow an alternating rhythm throughout the timeline (Scene 1 MUST always be a video to hook the user):
- Odd scenes (Scene 1, Scene 3, Scene 5, ...): MOTION VIDEO CLIP (<video_prompt[N]>)
- Even scenes (Scene 2, Scene 4, Scene 6, ...): STATIC IMAGE (<image_prompt[N]>)
Ensure exactly 50% of the scenes are designated as image assets and 50% as video assets.

## 🏷️ THE THREE-TAG MASTER PROTOCOL

The pipeline uses three and only three functional tag families:

1. **Narration Tag:** `<script>...</script>` — houses the complete, raw, TTS-ready English audio narration in Section 2B.
2. **Auto-Incrementing Visual Tags:** sequential visual prompts matching the exact timeline order across both static and moving formats:
   - `<image_prompt[N]>...</image_prompt[N]>` for static frames.
   - `<video_prompt[N]>...</video_prompt[N]>` for motion shots.
   - **Chronological Index Rule:** the index counter [N] increments chronologically across the entire video regardless of asset type: e.g., `<image_prompt1>`, `<video_prompt2>`, `<image_prompt3>`, `<video_prompt4>`.
3. **Thumbnail Tag:** always locked strictly to `<image_prompt0>...</image_prompt0>`. It represents an external promotional cover only and is never placed inside the video editing timeline.

**LOCKED FORMAT:** SHORT_IMAGE_VIDEO. **DURATION:** 45–70 seconds by default; up to 120 seconds when the selected duration requires it. The run request Target Duration overrides this default. **LANGUAGE:** English. **PLAYBACK ASPECT:** 9:16. **STYLE:** Grounded clean 2D animated-series frames; no photoreal or glossy 3D drift. **DEFAULT GENERATION MODE:** TEXT_ONLY_NO_REFERENCE across image and video models. If Cross-Model Mode is SHARED_REFERENCE_AVAILABLE, still copy all blocks verbatim, and additionally name the attached reference per asset in the prompt header.

## 📑 TABLE OF CONTENTS

1. WORKFLOW GUIDE — inputs, review, locking and assembly
2. THE BIBLE — rule/world logic, cast, locations, lore, modular continuity blocks and visual style
3. SCRIPT PROMPT — creative pass: Sections 1, 2 and 2B
4. PRODUCTION PROMPT — asset pass: Sections 3, 4 and 5

---

# PART 1 — 🧩 WORKFLOW GUIDE

## How to Use the Split System

### THE THREE WORKING PARTS

- **THE BIBLE:** Stable channel identity plus an episode-specific canon packet. Feed it to both passes.
- **THE SCRIPT PROMPT:** Produce an original story draft, scene lines with a Visible Subjects plan, timed narration and one complete script block wrapped in `<script>...</script>`. Do not produce image/video prompts yet.
- **THE PRODUCTION PROMPT:** Produce chronologically ordered visual prompts (`<image_prompt[N]>` and `<video_prompt[N]>`), overlays and publishing metadata from explicitly locked narration and the locked Visible Subjects plan. Never rewrite narration in the asset pass.

### WORKFLOW PER VIDEO

**STEP 1: PREPARE INPUTS**

```plaintext
Format: SHORT_IMAGE_VIDEO [fixed]
Target Duration: 45–70 seconds by default; up to 120 seconds when required (run request overrides)
Type: A (New World) / B (Same-World Episode) / C (Arc Expansion)
Rule: [One sentence, or GENERATE OPTIONS]
Title: [Optional working title]
Core Emotion: [Fear / curiosity / guilt / jealousy / hope / betrayal / love / survival]
Protagonist: [Ordinary person with a concrete goal]
Other Characters: [Name/role of each recurring or featured character, or NONE. Each needs a distinct design — see Cast Distinctness Rule]
Setting: [Ordinary room, street, school, station, cafe, office, apartment]
Premise / Content: [Optional story seed]
World ID / Episode ID: [New IDs or existing canon IDs]
Prior Canon: [Previously established rules, events, twists and unresolved questions; NONE for new world. For Type B/C this is REQUIRED — if missing, stop and ask]
Cross-Model Mode: TEXT_ONLY_NO_REFERENCE [default] / SHARED_REFERENCE_AVAILABLE
Image Generator: [Model/service if known, or UNKNOWN]
Video Generator: [Model/service if known, or UNKNOWN]
Character References: [Images/design sheets, or NONE]
Location / Object References: [Available references, or NONE]
Continuity Priority: [Face / outfit / location / symbol details that must never drift]
Lore Mode: NONE [default] / APPROVED_CAMEO / APPROVED_CONNECTION
Approved Lore: [Rulekeeper/symbol/organisation facts allowed in this episode]
Ending: Earned contradiction / discovery, with one new question
CTA: NONE [default] / Subscribe for more Rule Zero stories.
TTS Mode: PLAIN [default] / V2_SSML [only when supported]
Video Clip Budget: 3 [default; adjust with reason]
Channel Handle: [Confirmed handle, or NONE]
Constraints: [Budget, topic exclusions, model limitations, continuity requirements]
```

Note: there is no "episode scope" setting. Who or what is visible is decided shot by shot in the Script Pass.

For GENERATE OPTIONS, first return five original rule seeds, each with its one-line rule, visible symbol, ordinary-person dilemma and possible earned reveal. Do not output a full episode until a seed is selected. If a rule is already supplied, proceed without an unnecessary selection step.

**STEP 2: RUN SCRIPT PASS**
Provide this file's Parts 2 and 3 with your input packet. Receive Sections 1, 2 and 2B. Review rule clarity, emotional stakes, fair twist, canon, narration and the Visible Subjects plan. Draft status is DRAFT, then READY FOR REVIEW after internal revisions; only the user can explicitly lock it with `Script Status: LOCKED`.

**STEP 3: RUN ASSET PASS**
Provide Parts 2 and 4, locked script, locked Visible Subjects plan and the approved episode Bible. Receive Sections 3, 4 and 5. If the locked story contradicts canon or cannot be illustrated, report the issue before producing misleading assets; do not silently repair narration.

**STEP 4: GENERATE / EDIT**

- Extract only text inside `<script>` for speech. Outer tags are packaging, not TTS commands.
- For long narration, split at natural paragraph boundaries to fit current service limits. Preserve one full master script block; keep a chunk manifest to prevent gaps and repeated lines.
- Test pronunciation and performance before generating full narration. Timings remain estimates until audio exists.
- In TEXT_ONLY_NO_REFERENCE mode, create the Cast Bible, Location/Object Bible and all continuity blocks before any final asset generation. Treat those locked words as the reference system.
- Extract prompt payloads from `<image_prompt[N]>` and `<video_prompt[N]>` wrappers; packaging IDs must not appear as accidental image lettering.
- Assemble narration and assets in strict chronological index order; replace estimated timestamps with actual timings. Never place `<image_prompt0>` on the video timeline.

**STEP 5: CANON LOCK**
Publish-time canon changes are separate from script approval. Save world ID, final rule definition, revealed exceptions, character states (for every character), lore references and unresolved threads. Never quietly overwrite earlier episodes. A sequel's input must include this ledger.

---

# PART 2 — 🧩 THE BIBLE

## Channel Canon + Episode-Specific Reference

### 📺 CHANNEL IDENTITY

- Global English-language fiction: sci-fi mystery, psychological drama, speculative microdrama.
- Ordinary world + one impossible rule.
- Story, not a list of hypotheticals: follow a person (or people) whose goal clashes with the rule.
- The impossible element stands out because the rest of the world feels familiar.
- Every episode gives a new consequence or discovery, not a recycled premise with a different number.

### 📜 RULE / WORLD BIBLE — LOCK BEFORE WRITING

```plaintext
WORLD ID:
Rule in One Sentence:
What Everyone Believes:
Actual Mechanism Known to the Author:
Scope: [Who, where, when]
Trigger:
Observable Effect / Symbol:
Limits / Costs:
Society's Practical Adaptation: [How ordinary people behave because of the rule]
How Society Can Be SHOWN: [Choose from: arranged/empty space, repeated symbol, single background figure, wear/evidence, narration-only, crowd (max 1–2 shots). This turns the adaptation into visuals.]
What Can Be Measured:
Exceptions: [NONE or deliberately defined]
What Protagonist Knows at Start:
Reveal Allowed in This Episode:
What Must Remain Unknown:
Future Arc Possibilities: [Not automatically canon]
Continuity Restrictions:
```

Avoid vague rules that change whenever the plot needs help. A reveal can overturn society's interpretation; it cannot arbitrarily erase the established mechanism. If an exception is planned, define its conditions privately before writing and plant a visible, retrospectively understandable clue. Do not introduce a second unrelated supernatural power to solve the first rule.

### 👤 CAST BIBLE (one entry per character: C1, C2, C3 …)

```plaintext
CHARACTER ID: [C1 = protagonist; C2, C3 … = other characters]
Tier: [FULL (protagonist or major) / COMPACT (secondary) / SILHOUETTE (background figures, no individual face)]
Name / Age Range / Role:
Ordinary Goal:
Emotional Vulnerability:
Relationship to the Rule:
Relationship to Other Characters:
Knowledge at Start:
Choice / Cost in This Episode:
Face Geometry: [face shape, jaw, cheekbones, chin, forehead]
Skin Tone: [plain descriptive tone; keep wording fixed]
Eyes / Brows: [shape, colour, spacing, brow thickness/angle]
Nose / Mouth: [simple stable geometry; no beauty-language drift]
Hair Geometry: [colour, length, texture, part, fringe, tied/loose state]
Build / Height Impression / Posture:
Wardrobe Lock: [garment type, exact dominant colours, material, sleeve/fit, shoes]
Key Accessory Lock: [ONE preferred; exact side/placement/material/colour]
Identity Anchors: [5–8 short features that must remain invariant]
Motion-Safe Restrictions: [no micro-patterns, logos, complex jewellery, etc.]
CHARACTER BLOCK (locked wording — see Block Word Budgets)
Approved Reference Asset: [optional; NONE is valid and expected in text-only mode]
Expression Range:
State at End:
```

**CAST DISTINCTNESS RULE:** Every two characters who can appear in the same shot must differ in at least THREE of: silhouette, hair (colour/length/style), dominant clothing colour, height impression, key accessory. Keep the protagonist's dominant colour unique in the cast so they are spottable in a wide shot. Give each character a fixed frame side when paired (e.g., C1 frame-left, C2 frame-right) unless the script explicitly changes it, and state it in the prompt. Never describe two characters with the same descriptive words.

**BACKGROUND FIGURES / CROWD DESIGN RULE (only if used):** Crowds do not need identity continuity; they need **behaviour and symbol continuity**. Lock: simplified faces or turned-away heads; muted palette (charcoal, off-white, beige, muted blue only, no soft-red on crowd); two or three shared silhouettes; no individual hero faces; ONE shared rule behaviour (e.g., "everyone stands behind the painted line," "every hand holds the card at chest height"); fixed placement of the rule symbol in the environment. Keep the protagonist's dominant colour as the only accent in the crowd shot.

### 🏙️ LOCATION / OBJECT BIBLE

```plaintext
LOCATION ID:
Ordinary Setting:
Room / Street Geometry: [shape, scale, floor/wall material, ceiling/sky condition]
Fixed Camera Orientation Map: [what is frame-left, center, frame-right from the main axis]
Doors / Windows: [exact side, size, frame material, open/closed state]
Recurring Furniture / Structures: [exact placement and relative size]
Foreground Anchor:
Background Anchors: [2–4 stable objects that should recur]
Time / Light / Weather:
Key-Light Lock: [source, direction, warmth/coolness, shadow softness]
Palette Lock: [dominant environmental colours]
LOCATION BLOCK (locked wording — see Block Word Budgets)
Recurring Objects and Placement:
Rule-Related Object / Symbol: [shape, size, material, colour, mounting/placement]
RULE-OBJECT BLOCK (locked wording, with an entry per state, e.g., STATE A / STATE B)
Exact Display Text / Number / Timer State per story beat:
Changes Allowed by Scene:
Approved Reference Asset: [optional; NONE is valid]
```

### 🧬 LORE / CONTINUITY BIBLE

```plaintext
WORLD / ARC ID:
Prior Episode Facts:
Character Knowledge:
Audience Knowledge:
Unresolved Thread:
Approved Recurring Symbol / Rulekeeper Appearance:
Forbidden Premature Answers:
This Episode's New Canon:
Potential Ideas NOT YET CANON:
```

### 🎨 LOCKED VISUAL IDENTITY — STYLE 1: 2D GRAPHIC NOVEL THRILLER

Clean 2D graphic novel cel-shaded comic style, realistic adult human proportions, expressive psychological fear and tension, bold black charcoal and ink outlines of medium-thin weight, matte flat colour fills, two-step cel shading with one crisp shadow family, cold cyan moonlight through blinds contrasted with warm amber rim light, high-contrast chiaroscuro shadows, minimal surface texture, grounded mystery thriller atmosphere. No 3D render, no glossy CGI, no Pixar-style dolls, no photorealism.

Reference Palette: charcoal black #1A1A1D, cold rain teal #2E4B57, muted brick #8C473A, off-white parchment #EAE7E1, warning amber #D97706, alert crimson #C53030.

### 🧱 MODULAR CONTINUITY BLOCKS

Instead of one fixed string, the Bible defines small, independent, locked blocks. Each block is written once, approved, and then copied verbatim.

| Block | Contents | Target length |
|---|---|---|
| **CHARACTER BLOCK (FULL)** | face geometry, skin tone, eyes/brows, hair geometry, build, exact wardrobe with colours/materials, key accessory with side | 40–60 words |
| **CHARACTER BLOCK (COMPACT)** | silhouette, hair, dominant clothing colour, one accessory, height impression | 25–40 words |
| **CROWD BLOCK** | shared silhouettes, palette, turned/simplified faces, shared rule behaviour | 25–40 words |
| **LOCATION BLOCK** | geometry, door/window side, 2–4 background anchors, floor/wall material | 35–45 words |
| **RULE-OBJECT BLOCK** | shape, size, material, colour, placement, plus current state | 20–30 words per state |
| **RENDER BLOCK** | locked 2D rendering treatment (text below) | ~30 words |
| **LIGHT/TIME LINE** | time of day, key-light direction, colour temperature, shadow softness | 1 line (≈15 words) |

**RENDER BLOCK (copy verbatim):**
"clean grounded 2D animated-series frame; realistic adult human proportions; simple charcoal outlines of medium-thin weight; matte flat colour fills; two-step cel shading with one soft shadow family; minimal skin texture; muted charcoal, off-white, muted blue and muted beige palette with selective soft-red accents; no painterly texture, no glossy 3D, no photorealism."

(The long-form render description may remain in the Bible for reference, but only the compact RENDER BLOCK is pasted into prompts.)

### 🔧 SHOT CONTINUITY STRING — ASSEMBLY RULES

generatedAudio.narrationText:
In our world, every secret you keep turns your copper pendant into lead.

Minor fibs add mere ounces, but carrying a life-altering truth creates fifty pounds of crushing downward force.

Walking through the city, you can instantly see who lives in peace and who is suffocating under silence.

For three years, I have dragged this heavy metal across my collarbones.

The constant pressure has bruised my skin dark purple and fractured my posture.

My younger sister, Maya, begs me every day to confess, assuming I did something unforgivable.

She has no idea that the secret multiplying my pendant's weight is being kept for her.

Carrying someone else's truth multiplies the strain—the metal now splinters solid oak upon contact.

The weight crushes against my ribs, leaving me gasping for air on the floor.

Maya kneels beside me in tears, begging me to speak before the chain breaks my spine.

Looking into her eyes, I realize my silence will kill me before it protects her.

With my throat straining, I force the unsaid words into the open.

It wasn't my crime. Years ago, Maya caused the fatal crash, and I hid the memory to carry her guilt.

As the truth leaves my lips, the leaden mass vanishes and snaps back to weightless copper.

I sit up straight for the first time in three years, completely unburdened.

Honesty didn't destroy her—it freed us both. Subscribe for more Rule Zero stories.

# 📋 RESEARCH DOSSIER: THE ECHO WEIGHT

---

## 1. Verified Facts, Background & Key Data

### World Rules & Core Lore: The Echo Weight
* **The Artifact (The Echo Pendant):** Every citizen in this world is bound from adulthood to wear an etched, 2-inch tarnished copper pendant suspended from a heavy bronze-link chain around their neck [1]. The pendant cannot be removed by force or tools without causing lethal trauma to the wearer.
* **The Density Mechanism:** 
  * Under normal conditions, a truth-bound pendant weighs less than 2 ounces, resting weightlessly against the sternum.
  * When a wearer knowingly conceals a truth (a lie, a hidden act, or an unconfessed trauma), the internal structure of the copper changes physical density without expanding in physical volume [1].
  * Minor fibs add fractions of an ounce. Major, life-altering secrets alter the atomic lattice from hollow copper density to solid lead-equivalent mass, scaling up to 50+ pounds of downward gravitational pull [1].
* **The Paradox of Sacrificial Silence (The Secret Rules):**
  * Carrying an unspoken truth *to protect someone else* multiplies the kinetic strain [1]. Because the bearer is absorbing another person's moral debt, the universe punishes the silence with compounded density escalation.
  * The physical weight escalates continuously every 24 hours the truth remains unsaid, eventually causing cervical spine fractures, collarbone bruising, and asphyxiation [1].
* **The Confession Discharge:** 
  * The weight cannot be lifted by physical support, crutches, or hoists—the gravitational pull passes through objects, cracking wooden desks and stone floors upon contact [1].
  * The weight is only discharged when the exact, unvarnished truth is spoken aloud directly to the person affected or to an official arbiter [1]. Upon confession, the pendant instantly sheds its leaden mass with an acoustic resonance, returning to a weightless resting state [1].

### Target Viewer & Microdrama Context
* **Emotion:** *Sacrifice* (The agony of carrying a destructive truth for a loved one vs. the physical release of honesty) [1].
* **Protagonist Want:** To protect her younger sister from a ruinous past truth, even if the physical weight of that secret kills her [1].
* **Title Anchor:** *The World Where Secrets Weigh 50 Pounds* [1].

---

The weight has reached an unbearable 50 pounds [1]. | Wood creaking and cracking under the point-pressure of the small copper medallion [1]. |
| **Beat 5** | 00:52 - 01:08 | **The Confrontation** | Maya kneels beside Elena, crying and begging her to confess whatever crime or secret she is carrying before the neck chain breaks her spine [1]. | Intense emotional confrontation in warm amber lamp light; Elena weeping in silence [1]. |
| **Beat 6** | 01:08 - 01:22 | **The Climax & Earned Twist** | Elena collapses onto the cracked stone floor, barely able to breathe. She reveals the twist: the secret isn't Elena's crime—she was protecting Maya from knowing Maya caused a fatal accident years ago. Elena whispers the raw truth aloud [1]. | Low-angle camera looking up at Elena speaking the exact truth into Maya's eyes [1]. |
| **Beat 7** | 01:22 - 01:30 | **Payoff & Resolution** | As the final word is spoken, the pendant glows faintly copper and instantly becomes weightless. Elena sits up straight for the first time in years as the sisters embrace [1]. | Kinetic release sound effect; chain slackens instantly; emotional release [1]. |

---

## 3. Visual & World-Building Canon

### Setting & Environment
* **Architectural Style:** Grounded, realistic 2D animated aesthetic with muted urban tones (industrial European/Ghibli-inspired low-tech realism) [1]. Dark polished wood desks, cracked cobblestone floors, worn brick interiors [1].
* **Lighting & Atmosphere:** High contrast between warm interior desk lamps (amber/gold) and cold exterior street lighting (indigo/slate) [1]. Deep shadow casting beneath heavy objects to emphasize weight and downward force [1].

### Character Canon & Visual Anchor Specifications
* **Elena (Protagonist):**
  * *Age & Build:* Late 20s, gaunt frame, visibly stooped posture from chronic spinal strain [1].
  * *Wardrobe:* Oversized dark navy wool coat, coarse knit cream sweater, thick wool scarf tucked around the neck to hide purple pressure bruises [1].
  * *Hair & Face:* Dark chestnut hair tied in a loose low bun with stray strands framing a pale, exhausted face; dark shadows under hollow eyes [1].
* **Maya (Younger Sister):**
  * *Age & Build:* Early 20s, vibrant posture, perfectly straight spine [1].
  * *Wardrobe:* Warm mustard-yellow knit sweater, clean denim trousers [1].
  * *Hair & Face:* Bright hazel eyes, soft feature structure, hair loose over shoulders [1].

### Key Prop Canon: The Echo Pendant
* **Visual Specifications:** 2-inch diameter circular medallion made of patinated, teal-tinged tarnished copper [1]. Etched with concentric circular soundwave grooves across the face [1].
* **Chain Specifications:** Interlocking dark bronze metal links, 0.5 inches thick [1]. When under load, the chain flattens taut against skin, indenting clothing and wood surfaces [1].

---

## 4. Scriptwriter Directives

* **Mandatory Opening Line:** The narration MUST begin precisely with: *"In our world, every secret you keep turns your copper pendant into lead."* [1]
* **Key Narrative Mechanics to Maintain:**
  1. The pendant changes mass/density, not size [1].
  2. The weight increases exponentially when keeping a truth to protect someone else [1].
  3. The physical weight affects inanimate objects (cracking wood desks, denting floors) [1].
  4. The only resolution is speaking the literal truth out loud to the person involved [1].
* **Pacing & Tone:** Tone must be emotionally grounded, urgent, and empathetic. Avoid technical jargon or comedic breaks. Focus on the physical sensory details of heavy metal, strained neck muscles, creaking wood, and the sudden lightness of confession [1].
* **Ending Resolution:** Ensure the CTA or closing beat occurs *after* the emotional release and truth resolution are fully shown on screen [1].

In a world where unspoken truths add literal physical weight to an etched copper neck pendant, Elena carries 50 pounds of crushing density to protect her younger sister from a tragic past. As the gravity threatens her collarbones and spine, she faces an impossible choice: confess the truth or be crushed by silence.
